name: @fuzdev/tsv-benches
description: tsv benchmark harness deps — the single source of truth for the npm package versions the bench measures against. Consumed by BOTH runtimes: Deno reads it via `nodeModulesDir: "manual"` in deno.json, Node reads it directly. Install with `npm install` (the one installer). The jsr-only `@std/*` packages, if any, stay in deno.json.
//canonical-sync: ⚠ The 5 canonical packages (prettier, svelte, acorn, @sveltejs/acorn-typescript, prettier-plugin-svelte) are ALSO pinned as literals in crates/tsv_debug/src/deno/sidecar.ts and resolved by the sidecar lockfile crates/tsv_debug/src/deno/deno.lock, and all three MUST match — agreement (and ../svelte / ../acorn-typescript checkout alignment, when present) is enforced by `deno task pins:audit` (scripts/check_canonical_pins.ts, in `deno task check`). Bumping any re-baselines the whole fixture corpus — see docs/benchmarks.md §'Canonical baseline is coupled'. The other deps (oxc, oxfmt, biome, etc.) are free to bump independently. ⚠ This lockfile's TRANSITIVE versions are NOT part of that contract and are deliberately not synced: `esrap` here sits at whatever npm resolved for svelte's caret range, which can differ from the sidecar lock's pin. That is fine — nothing in this harness ever calls svelte's `compile()` (lib/canonical.ts uses `parse`/`parseCss` only, and the reject cache is a PARSE harvest), so esrap is loaded but never invoked and cannot move a measured number. The sidecar lock is the authoritative pin because it is the one that decides oracle OUTPUT; aligning this file to it would mean an `overrides` entry plus an `npm install` that prunes the oxc wasi binding and can churn the measured toolchain, i.e. all risk and no effect.
//engines: Node ≥ 22.18 is the native TS type-stripping floor — the harness entries (bench.ts, install_deps.ts) run as TypeScript directly under `node`. Advisory (npm warns without engine-strict); an older Node fails with an opaque parse error before any runtime guard could fire.
//typescript: tsc (the last JS implementation — 6.x; 7.x is the Go port, whose npm package ships a binary with no in-process parser API) plays two roles here, both PARSE-only: the validity ORACLE for the tsc-corpus harvest (harvest_ts_repo.ts) and a parser ROW in the TS bench group (lib/tsc.ts). One definitional asymmetry to remember: tsc's parser is ERROR-RECOVERING — `createSourceFile` never throws, it returns a SourceFile plus `parseDiagnostics` — so an accept here means `parseDiagnostics.length === 0`, not `didn't throw`. Not one of the canonical-5 (nothing in the fixture corpus is baselined against it), so it bumps independently; keep it in the same MAJOR as the ../typescript checkout the corpus comes from, since a version below the corpus rejects the syntax the newer tests were written for.
//types: @types/node is types-only and dev-only (never ships, no runtime cost). It lets the shared harness's `node:` builtins type-check under `deno check` (and editors) when an npm package's .d.ts pulls in node types in npm-resolution mode — the portable-node:-builtins architecture's one new dev dep. NOT needed by the gated `deno task test:deno` (that's the dependency-free divergence suite — `node:assert` + relative imports, no node_modules).
//rsvelte: @rsvelte/fmt is a CLI, not a library — the npm package is a Node launcher and the real formatter is a prebuilt binary carried by a platform `optionalDependency` (@rsvelte/fmt-<triple>), which is what lib/rsvelte.ts execs directly. Listing the launcher package is what pulls the right platform binary in; nothing imports it. Its only hard dep is prettier-plugin-tailwindcss (no transitive tree of its own), and its `oxfmt` peer is optional and unused here — .svelte formatting never leaves the binary. Because it has no in-process API its bench row is COVERAGE-ONLY (never timed) — see lib/rsvelte.ts and docs/benchmarks.md §Coverage-only rows.
//yuku: yuku-parser (N-API) and @yuku-parser/wasm are one Zig parser behind two bindings, versioned in lockstep — bump both together. Unlike the oxc wasi binding, the wasm package declares no `cpu`/`os`, so it installs as an ordinary dep on every host; the native package pulls its platform binary through `optionalDependencies` like oxc/oxfmt do. Both are PARSE-only (TS/JS — no Svelte, no CSS, no formatter), so they contribute rows to `parse/typescript` alone. Two properties of its JS API decide how lib/yuku.ts must drive it: `parse()` is LAZY (the AST materializes only when `.program` is read — a 1.69x/1.91x measured cost) and the parser is ERROR-TOLERANT (it never throws; an invalid file yields an empty AST plus `diagnostics`). One wrapper class drives both bindings, so both rows force `.program` and read `.diagnostics` by construction — see docs/benchmarks.md §Fairness caveats.
//oxc-wasi: The oxc-parser WASM bench row needs @oxc-parser/binding-wasm32-wasi — pure-wasm (runtime-portable) but its metadata declares `cpu: wasm32`, so npm skips it on any non-wasm host. It is NOT listed as a dep here: declaring it errors on x64, and as an optionalDependency npm records it as known-skipped so a later `--force` reinstall no-ops. Instead `deno task bench:install` (install_deps.ts) force-fetches it at the oxc-parser version (oxc ships all bindings in lockstep), so the `oxc-parser` pin above is its single source of truth too.
